([[Danvers, Massachusetts]]) | college = [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] (2011–2015) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Third-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] ([[2014–15 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|2015]]) }} '''Patrick (The Bull) Connaughton''' (born January 6, 1993) is an American [[professional baseball]] and [[college basketball|NCAA basketball]] player who has exhausted his [[National Collegiate Athletic Association#Eligibility|eligibility]]. He is a member of the [[Baltimore Orioles]] organization in [[Minor League Baseball]] as a [[pitcher]] and had played for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball]] team as a [[guard (basketball)|guard]] and a [[forward (basketball)|forward]], including in a 2015 tournament game against the [[2014–15 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|University of Kentucky]] for a [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Final Four]] berth, narrowly lost by his team after having sustained a prolonged lead until the 6-second mark. He is to graduate in Spring 2015. ==High school== Connaughton attended [[St. John's Preparatory School (Danvers, Massachusetts)|St. John's Preparatory School]] in [[Danvers, Massachusetts]], where he starred in three sports, playing [[quarterback]] in [[American football|football]] and multiple positions in both baseball and basketball.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12133309/notre-dame-fighting-irish-senior-pat-connaughton-dual-sport-athlete-torn-basketball-baseball |title=Connaughton's dual-sport decision |first=Jeff |last=Goodman |publisher=''[[ESPN.com]]'' |date=January 9, 2015 |accessdate=January 9, 2015}} He received major interest in baseball from schools in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]], with [[Boston College]] (BC), the [[University of Virginia]], and his original first choice, the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], who all made him scholarship offers. Connaughton's sporting trajectory changed during the summer between his junior and senior years. At that time, he had only received a basketball offer from home-state [[Bentley University]], in NCAA's [[Division II (NCAA)|Division II]]. He suddenly emerged as a major basketball prospect after what ''[[ESPN.com]]'' writer Jeff Goodman called "one spectacular week" at the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] national tournament in [[Orlando, Florida]], including a game where he had 33 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 20 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]]. Connaughton himself would later say, "That week completely changed my entire life." He then began receiving multiple offers in basketball as well as baseball, with many schools willing to let him play both sports. He eventually chose the [[University of Notre Dame]] over BC, the [[University of Miami]], the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], and [[Vanderbilt University]]. In 2011, Connaughton's senior year, he was named the [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Massachusetts Boys Basketball Player of the Year]].{{cite web|url=http://www.boston.com/yourtown/news/danvers/2011/03/pat_connaughton_is_the_gatorad.html|title=Pat Connaughton is the Gatorade Massachusetts Boys Basketball Player of the Year|first=Ayoub |last=Kourikchi|work=Boston Globe|date=March 18, 2011|accessdate=June 13, 2014}} As a [[pitcher]] for the baseball team, he had a 11–2 [[win–loss record (pitching)|win–loss record]] with a 1.75 [[earned run average]] (ERA) and 160 [[strikeout]]s in 90 [[innings pitched]] as a senior. According to the baseball scouting site ''Perfect Game'', Connaughton was rated as the 33rd-best player in [[2011 Major League Baseball Draft|that year's]] [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB) [[Major League Baseball draft|draft]], but he fell to the 38th round, where he was selected by the [[San Diego Padres]], when he made it clear he planned to attend college. He followed through on his commitment to Notre Dame, choosing not to sign with the Padres. ==Collegiate career== At Notre Dame, Connaughton joined the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] as a member of their [[college baseball]] and [[college basketball]] teams. In [[2011–12 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|his freshman year]] for the basketball team, Connaughton was one of three players to appear in all of Notre Dame's 34 games. He averaged 7.0 [[points per game]] (PPG), 4.4 [[rebounds per game]], and 0.9 [[assists per game]] while playing 24.1 [[minutes per game]]. The Fighting Irish appeared in the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]], but lost to [[2011–12 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier University]] in the second round. Connaughton scored 10 points with two assists and two rebounds in 34 minutes of play during the loss. He then joined the baseball team as a [[relief pitcher]].{{cite web|url=http://articles.southbendtribune.com/2012-03-20/news/31217705_1_dame-freshman-pat-connaughton-eck-stadium-first-pitch|title=Notre Dame baseball: Connaughton brings the heat|first=Tom|last=Noie|work=[[South Bend Tribune]]|date=March 20, 2012|accessdate=January 11, 2015}} As a sophomore, in 2013, Connaughton averaged 8.9 PPG for the basketball team, and had a 1.71 ERA for the baseball team.{{cite web|url=http://www.fortwayne.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/FW/20130325/SPORTS/320131770/1002|title=New league will bring new challenges for Irish|first=Tony|last=Krausz career at Notre Dame, even if MLB Draft calls|first=Scott |last=Phillips|work=CollegeBasketballTalk|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|date=May 29, 2014|accessdate=January 11, 2015}} In the summer of 2013, he web|url=http://articles.southbendtribune.com/2013-06-13/sports/39960131_1_notre-dame-baseball-pat-connaughton-debut|title=Notre Dame baseball: Connaughton makes debut|work=South Bend Tribune|date=June 13, 2013|accessdate=January 11, 2015}} In his junior year, he averaged 13.8 PPG for the basketball team and had a 3.92 ERA in ten [[games started]], which included two [[complete game]]s, for the baseball team.{{cite web|url=http://www.southbendtribune.com/sports/professional/notre-dame-two-sport-athlete-connaughton-reaches-deal-with-orioles/article_333107f6-f081-11e3-ba1d-0017a43b2370.html|title=Notre Dame two-sport athlete Connaughton reaches deal with Orioles|work=South Bend Tribune|date=June 10, 2014|accessdate=January 11, 2015}} After his junior year, he was forthright about his intent to return to Notre Dame for his senior basketball season, despite warnings that it would impact his prospects for the upcoming baseball draft.{{cite news|last=Benbow|first=Julian|title=Pat Connaughton chose to stay at Notre Dame|date=March 26, 2015|newspaper=The Boston 2015|deadurl=no}} He was drafted by the [[Baltimore Orioles]] of [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB) in the fourth round, with the 121st overall selection, of the [[2014 MLB Draft]].{{cite web|last=Norlander |first=Matt |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24582190/notre-dame-g-pat-connaughton-drafted-as-pitcher-by-baltimore-orioles |title=Notre Dame G Pat Connaughton taken by Baltimore Orioles in MLB Draft |publisher=CBSSports.com |date=June 6, 2014 |accessdate=June 13, 2014}}{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2014-06-06/sports/chi-connaughton-notre-dame-orioles-20140606_1_notre-dame-orioles-draft |title=Orioles draft Pat Connaughton|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|first=Chris|last=Hine|date=June 6, 2014|accessdate=June 13, 2014}} One high-ranking MLB executive believed that Connaughton would have been drafted in the first two rounds had he not been committed to returning to Notre Dame for his senior basketball season, telling Goodman, "He definitely cost himself some money," as he expected Connaughton could have earned $1 million if he was willing to quit basketball. He agreed to terms with the Orioles, receiving a signing bonus of over $400,000, with the Orioles permitting Connaughton to play basketball for the Irish in his senior year.{{cite web|url=http://www.si.com/basketball/2014/06/09/pat-connaughton-baltimore-orioles-contract-notre-dame |title=Orioles to allow Pat Connaughton to play basketball for Notre Dame|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 9, 2014 |accessdate=June 13, 2014}}{{cite web|agency=Associated Press|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/2014/06/09/notre-dames-pat-connaughton-will-play-two-sports/10260889/ |title=Notre Dame's Pat Connaughton will play two sports |work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=June 9, 2014 |accessdate=June 13, 2014}} As a senior, Notre Dame's basketball team won its first [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) championship. He took part in a 2015 tournament game against Kentucky for a [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Final Four]] berth, narrowly lost by his team after having sustained a prolonged lead until the 6-second mark. He is to graduate in Spring 2015. ==Professional baseball career== Connaughton made his [[professional baseball]] debut with the [[Aberdeen IronBirds]] of the [[Class A-Short Season]] [[New York–Penn League]], in which he registered a {{convert|96|mph}} [[fastball]].{{cite web|url=http://www.southbendtribune.com/sports/professional/pro-baseball-connaughton-makes-professional-debut/article_05292dea-029a-11e4-9c8c-001a4bcf6878.html|title=Pro baseball: Connaughton makes professional debut|work=South Bend Tribune|accessdate=January 11, 2015}} At the end of July 2014, he left the IronBirds to return to the Fighting Irish basketball team.{{cite web|url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/orioles/bs-sp-orioles-pat-connaughton-0726-20140725-story.html|title=For Aberdeen's Pat Connaughton, baseball to take backseat this week |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|first=Alejandro |last=Zuniga|date=July 29, 2014|accessdate=January 11, 2015}} ==Personal life== In Goodman's 2015 story on Connaughton and his decision between two sports, many key individuals in his life testified to his character. His father Len noted, "Patrick is of high moral character and wasn't going to lie to people. That eliminated a bunch of [MLB] teams from taking him at all." Notre Dame head basketball coach [[Mike Brey]] added, "In my 15 years here, no one has been more responsible than Pat Connaughton. He's an unbelievable ambassador for us and has shown tremendous loyalty." Family adviser Sam Samardzija, father of current [[Chicago White Sox]] pitcher and former Notre Dame baseball and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|football]] star [[Jeff Samardzija]], said about Connaughton, "He's not common—kind of like Jeff and [NFL quarterback] [[Russell Wilson]]. Not a lot of guys like him come around. He's just wired differently." Connaughton only allowed himself one luxury with his signing bonus, buying a new [[Jeep Wrangler]]. He told Goodman, "The signing bonus is a ton of money, especially for a 21-year-old. But I'm not going to live off that money. At some point, I'm going to live off a college degree." Connaughton is determined to finish his degree at Notre Dame, and he has a 3.0 [[Grading (education)|grade point average]] with the university's [[Mendoza College of Business]].
